But often, that is not enough: even if all the atoms stay exactly where they are, the distribution of electric charge within the material can change dramatically. items.title: Stromal mitochondrial reprogramming and transfer reveal a chemotherapy-associated tumor state in ovarian cancer
items.blurb: Mitochondrial transfer from stromal cells promotes ovarian cancer progression, yet the functional state of donor mitochondria remains poorly understood. Here we define a stress-adapted mitochondrial state in carcinoma-associated mesenchymal stem cells (CA-MSCs), characterized by increased respiratory and glycolytic activity despite increased mitochondrial proton leak and inefficient coupling of respiration to ATP production, oxidative stress, and elevated mitochondrial DNA variant burden. We identify WT1 as a regulator of mitochondrial reprogramming and PDK4 as a metabolic adaptation critical for CA-MSC growth. We further show that CA-MSCs preferentially transfer highly oxidized mitochondria to ovarian cancer cells. In a freshly-dissociated primary high grade serous ovarian cancer patient tumor, using mitochondrial variant tracking, we identify a transcriptionally distinct tumor population sharing mitochondrial variant patterns with stroma, in line with stromal-tumor mitochondrial transfer. This transcriptional signature is enriched in residual tumors following chemotherapy across four independent patient cohorts. Together, these findings establish stromal mitochondrial reprogramming and the preferential transfer of oxidatively-stressed mitochondria as important features of ovarian cancer heterogeneity and persistence following chemotherapy.

items.title: De Novo-Designed Alpha-Helical Proteins Enable Ligand-Directed Spectral Tuning
items.blurb: Canonical green fluorescent proteins typically regulate chromophore photophysics through a rigid beta-barrel environment, while spectral tuning often relies on protein engineering or directed evolution. Here, we design a compact alpha-helical protein pocket that activates a GFP-chromophore-derived fluorogen and accommodates a series of chemically modified ligands. A co-crystal structure reveals shared anchoring interactions for fluorogen activation and contacts that enable ligand-dependent spectral tuning. Guided by this structure, ligand substitution shifts emission across the red-to-green range while retaining the same protein scaffold. Quantitative binding and photophysical analyses establish the structural and chemical determinants of affinity, fluorescence activation, and spectral tuning, and the resulting fluorogens function in living cells. Finally, structure-guided substitutions repurpose the pocket toward a distinct drug ligand. These results establish an alpha-helical route to programmable fluorogen activation in which optical properties can be tuned through ligand design rather than repeated protein evolution.

items.title: Input Construction Accounts for Most PoseBusters Clash Failures on RNA-Ligand Complexes
items.blurb: PoseBusters, a widely used test of the physical validity of ligand poses, was calibrated on protein-ligand crystal structures, and whether its checks transfer to RNA has not been measured. Applied without filtering the input to 2,970 deposited RNA-ligand poses, the receptor-clash check failed 527 of 2,931 (18.0%), and all but 7 of the failures were in covalently bonded nucleotides or in entries that contain protein, were solved by cryo-electron microscopy or were resolved at worse than 2.0 [A], so most failures are associated with which structures and ligand records entered the input set. On a high-resolution set constructed after these failures were attributed, the check failed 3 of 149 (2.01%; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.00-4.58%) against 0.32% for the protein benchmark, a difference this set cannot resolve, and the PoseBusters calibration rule selected a threshold of 0.735 against the shipped 0.75. We give a seven-step dataset construction protocol and a tool, rnaprep, that implements its first four steps. On 139 redocking targets, with accuracy measured in the crystal frame without superposition, requiring a valid pose cost NucleoDock 25.2 points (69.06% to 43.88% within 2 [A]) and AutoDock Vina none, and cut the lead of NucleoDock from 38.9 points (95% CI 26.5-50.0) to 13.7 points, a lead not clearly distinguishable from zero (95% CI 1.3-27.5; cluster permutation P = 0.053). For these two programs in one redocking regime, the result supports reporting validity alongside RMSD in RNA docking benchmarks.

items.title: Distance-stratified benchmarking of variant-effect predictors on β-lactamase deep mutational scanning data
items.blurb: Mutations far from the active site of antibiotic-resistance enzymes can change resistance, but it is unclear what information predicts their effects. We asked how the performance of a protein language model (ESM2), a structure-based stability predictor (ThermoMPNN) and simple structural descriptors changes with distance from the catalytic residues, using deep mutational scanning data for the {beta}-lactamases TEM-1 (four assays) and VIM-2 (one assay). We measured Spearman correlation and AUROC within distance bins, with bootstrap intervals over positions. In TEM-1, ESM2 accuracy fell with distance (Stiffler assay: {rho} = 0.72 below 8 [A] and 0.42 beyond 20 [A]), while the stability score rose ({rho} = 0.41 to 0.70). Adding stability to a model of ESM2, solvent accessibility and neighbour count improved cross-validated {rho} by 0.02 below 8 [A] and 0.10 beyond 20 [A], and the combined model did not decline with distance. The pattern held across binning schemes, in a continuous-distance model, and when any one of five contiguous distal stretches was removed. Two TEM-1 assays are nearly duplicates, and the Deng assay was too noisy to be informative. VIM-2 has only seven positions beyond 20 [A] and showed no detectable trend within 20 [A], so it neither supports nor contradicts the TEM-1 pattern. Nine distal TEM-1 positions remained more sensitive than the models predicted. In TEM-1, predicted stability was more informative than the language model far from the catalytic site, and the language model was stronger near it. Distance-stratified reporting could add to variant-effect benchmarks. The study is exploratory and uses one structure and one phenotype per assay.

items.title: Standard benchmarking inflates gene-prioritization accuracy estimates
items.blurb: Benchmark results tell clinics which gene-prioritization system to trust and the field what counts as progress. Standard benchmarking practice --- testing each system using its latest knowledge databases --- can inflate system accuracy estimates and invite data leakage. We formalize the Fairbench protocol: testing may use only knowledge available strictly before the patient's assessment. Against prepublication snapshots dated by case report, on one public case collection, standard benchmarking inflated Top-1 accuracy by 40.5--80.5 percentage points across Exomiser, LIRICAL, Phrank and Phen2Disease. In every system, over half the tested patients had a causal-gene phenotype association whose only recorded source was their case publication. Reassessing three systems' published benchmarks with reproduced or reconstructed references showed the same direction in all five comparisons. Retesting undiagnosed patients with the latest knowledge database is good care. But benchmark results are read as performance at the patient's assessment, and Fairbench is a necessary data-hygiene condition for that reading.

items.title: StarCrew: A pipeline for exploratory analysis of Starship cargo
items.blurb: BackgroundStarships are giant cargo-mobilizing mobile elements within the fungal subphylum Pezizomycotina that harbor diverse gene content, including genes for virulence and heavy metal resistance. Although Starship elements carry a vast array of cargo genes, the overall composition and function of this cargo remain largely uncharacterized for most elements. While existing bioinformatic tools have been designed for the identification of these elements, a gap remains in tools for characterizing their gene content while accounting for its specific characteristics. ResultsTo address the gap in gene content analysis of Starships, we present StarCrew, a bash- based pipeline designed for systematically characterizing the cargo gene diversity and turnover within Starship elements. We demonstrate that StarCrew robustly handles datasets of varying diversity, providing the capacity to cluster elements based on collinear regions, identify nested insertion events, perform element classification, and highlight overrepresented genes within a dataset. Additionally, StarCrew serves as a diagnostic tool to flag elements requiring boundary curation. We found that the accuracy of the pipeline was sensitive to the quality of input gene models and the precision of initial element boundaries delineation. Demonstrating its utility, we identified a putative pseudokinase as a new conserved protein distributed across Starships. ConclusionsStarCrew provides a practical and versatile resource for the continuous exploration of Starship gene content, designed to adapt alongside our expanding understanding of these mobile elements. Finally, we propose a complementary system to group elements with potential shared beneficial traits, based on collinear blocks, called Functional Constellations.

items.title: SPECTRAM: three-dimensional full-vector simulation of coherence-tunable microscopy images
items.blurb: We present SPECTRAM, a physics-based framework for three-dimensional simulation of coherence-tunable microscopy image formation. Combining finite-difference time-domain solutions of Maxwell's equations with a coherence-tunable, polarization-dependent image-formation model, SPECTRAM captures full-vector light scattering and modality-specific optical processing in brightfield, differential interference contrast, and phase-contrast microscopy. It supports arbitrary three-dimensional sample geometries and generates volumetric image stacks under configurable illumination and objective parameters. Validated against Mie theory and experimental images of polystyrene beads, SPECTRAM further reproduces imaging features of an iPSC-derived stem cell using a refractive-index distribution estimated by gradient light interference microscopy. SPECTRAM provides a versatile, physics-based tool for quantitative three-dimensional simulation of phase-sensitive microscopy.

items.title: Programming Continuous, High Framerate, and Long-Duration Data Acquisitions on the Verasonics Ultrasound System
items.blurb: The ultrasound community has seen a rise in popularity of highly demanding imaging acquisition sequences, such as those for super-resolution ultrasound localization microscopy and functional ultrasound imaging, which push the boundary of ultrasound system hardware limits. However, subtle errors in sequence programming can lead to corrupted data, inaccurate timing, and slow data throughput, which impact the performance of these modalities. In this article, we detail the fundamentals of the hardware and software sequencers for the Verasonics Vantage/NXT research ultrasound scanner, highlighting some common pitfalls in sequence design and ways to overcome them. We include example imaging sequences for different data acquisition goals, and detail recommended ways to test these sequences to ensure that they are meeting the expected performance.

items.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the hydrozoan jellyfish Cladonema pacificum
items.blurb: The hydrozoan jellyfish Cladonema pacificum, which possesses experimentally tractable polyp and medusa stages, is an emerging cnidarian model for studies of regeneration, development, physiology, and behavior. Although experimental techniques have been established for this species, the lack of a chromosome-level reference genome has limited genome-wide and comparative analyses. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of C. pacificum generated using HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C technology. The representative haploid assembly comprises 15 chromosome-scale scaffolds and 121 additional scaffolds, spanning 504.0 Mb with a scaffold N50 of 32.1 Mb. Gene annotation integrating RNA-seq, PacBio Iso-Seq, and protein homology identified 17,206 protein-coding genes, of which 95.7% received at least one functional annotation. Phylogenomic and macrosynteny analyses further confirmed the placement of C. pacificum within Hydrozoa and revealed extensive chromosome-scale conservation with other hydrozoan genomes. This genomic resource provides a valuable foundation for comparative genomics and future molecular, cellular, and evolutionary studies using C. pacificum as an emerging hydrozoan model.

items.title: A gene-edited chicken model of ocular coloboma reveals Netrin-1 is required for pioneer cell detachment during optic fissure closure
items.blurb: Coloboma, a leading cause of childhood blindness, results from failed OFC. Variants in NTN1 (Netrin-1) are linked to coloboma and other tissue fusion defects, but how Netrin-1 influences epithelial fusion is unknown. We generated a germline NTN1 knockout chicken and analysed the fissure margins by immunofluorescence, in situ hybridisation, single-nucleus RNA sequencing and micro-CT. NTN1-/- embryos developed highly penetrant bilateral colobomas. The basement membrane (BM) was remodelled normally, yet pioneer cells at the optic fissure margins (OFMs) failed to detach and mix across the midline, retaining apical actin and displaying increased cadherin at the fissure edges. The ventral neural retina showed reduced apoptosis and became overgrown and folded at the fissure edges. These data show that Netrin-1 is required for pioneer cell detachment and this process is independent of BM remodelling. We found that pioneer cells in wild type (WT) OFMs were transiently exposed to fibronectin-rich periocular mesenchyme (POM) during BM remodelling, with fibronectin and laminin fragments localised at their exposed edges. Netrin-1 reduced adhesion of HEK293 cells to fibronectin in vitro, with and without laminin, but not to laminin alone, suggesting Netrin-1 mediates a substrate specific effect on cell adhesion. ITGB8 and ITGAV were co-expressed with NTN1 in pioneer cells, and Netrin-1 co-immunoprecipitated with ITGB8, identifying integrin V{beta}8 as a candidate Netrin-1 receptor in OFC. Integrin V{beta}8 with fibronectin typically activate canonical TGF{beta} signalling, however we found pSMAD2 was specifically absent from pioneer cell nuclei during fusion. In contrast, phosphorylated FAK was present in WT but not mutant fissures, indicating that Netrin-1 activates integrin mediated focal adhesion signalling in OFC. We propose that Netrin-1 and V{beta}8 enable pioneer cells to respond to transient POM-derived cues, such as fibronectin, triggering detachment and initiating fusion. This proposed mechanism could explain a direct role for the POM in mediating OFC.

items.title: Transient telomerase mRNA delivery extends the proliferative capacity of patient-derived Duchenne muscular dystrophy myogenic progenitors
items.blurb: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disease, characterised by progressive skeletal and cardiac muscle degeneration and impaired regeneration. Repeated regenerative cycles contribute to muscle stem cell exhaustion, potentially driven by telomere shortening under chronic proliferative demand. Here, we tested whether transient delivery of hTERT mRNA can increase the relative telomere signal (Q-FISH) in patient-derived DMD myogenic progenitors (CD56+) and interstitial (CD56-) cells from two DMD donors, compared with one control donor. hTERT mRNA treatment increased the relative telomere signal and added 2 to 6 population doublings in DMD myogenic progenitors, whereas healthy donor cells showed no comparable benefit in proliferation. Exploratory transcriptomic analysis indicated genotype-associated differences in translation- and cell-cycle-related gene sets following hTERT treatment. Telomere elongation and improved proliferation were not accompanied by recovery of myogenic differentiation; no karyotypic abnormalities were detected under the conditions tested. By transiently increasing the proliferative output of dystrophic cells without genomic integration, this proof of concept provides a basis for further investigation of telomere-associated proliferative limits in DMD and a starting point for future regenerative approaches.

items.title: Rare Epithelial Sentinel Cells Establish Functional Domains of the Airway
items.blurb: Organs exposed to the environment must sense threats in order to evoke protective physiologic responses. Recent single-cell sequencing studies of the airway epithelium have led to the identification of a suite of rare epithelial cells, many of which are unified by their ability to sense stimuli1,2. Herein, we explore how organized networks of epithelial sentinel cells transduce distinct stimuli to alter tissue function by employing a combination of cell type-specific calcium indicators, optogenetics, chemogenetics, cell ablation, and live ACh and ATP sensors. We define a new diversity of functional sentinel cells including 3 new subtypes of chemosensory tuft cells. We further show that solitary neuroendocrine cells, like their tuft cell counterparts, generate stimulus-induced waves of calcium activation. These waves originate from a central sentinel cell and expand outwards to encompass a circular domain of surrounding epithelial cells. We demonstrate that basolateral secretion and diffusion of neurotransmitters cause the activation of the surrounding epithelial effector cells including basal stem cells which were not previously known to be participants in sentinel cell-induced calcium waves. We show that these diffusion-limited domains (DLDs) are generated by specific patterns of ACh and ATP secretion characteristic of specific sentinel cell populations. The speed, intensity, and domain size of DLDs are dictated by the degree of stimulus-triggered neurotransmitter secretion. Thus, DLDs represent a unified mechanism for specifying functional domains within the airway epithelium. Triggered sentinel cells generate surrounding circular domains of increased mucociliary transport and enhance stem cell replication. Insulated sentinel cell networks are tuned to distinct stimuli. Sentinel cells are distributed in sufficient numbers to ensure comprehensive epithelial coverage. However, the amplitude and number of DLDs scale with stimulus intensity, permitting both local and global physiologic activation of the epithelium. Additionally, the distribution of sentinel cells can vary with organ anatomy, resulting in compartmentalized physiologic responses. Furthermore, cytokines modulate DLD responses. IL-1{beta} amplifies ciliary action by generating larger and more intense DLDs, while IFN-{gamma} reduces the density of DLDs by directly depleting sentinel cells. Finally, we show that a fungal metabolite triggers DLDs. In aggregate, we reveal a sophisticated collective of diverse sentinel cells that activate surrounding circular domains of airway epithelium to generate protective responses to environmental threats.

items.title: Dual-loop DogTag engineering enables modular antigen display on human vault nanoparticles
items.blurb: Self-assembling protein nanoparticles can enhance immune responses by displaying multiple copies of an antigen on their surface. Most previous studies using vault nanoparticles have focused on loading proteins inside the particle or modifying its ends. Here, we introduced two DogTag peptides into separate surface-exposed loops of human major vault protein (MVP), creating up to 156 potential attachment sites on each 78-subunit vault. The engineered MVP formed vault-sized particles in suspension HEK cells, to which separately produced, stabilized influenza H5N1 Clade 2.3.4.4b hemagglutinin (HA) fused to DogCatcher was covalently attached. By varying the amount of HA added, we obtained preparations with estimated loadings of approximately 32, 64, and 124 HA trimers per vault. Structural models showed that increasing HA loading reduced the median distance between neighboring HA trimers from 13.3 to 8.8 nm, while electron microscopy showed that highly loaded particles retained their characteristic vault morphology. Following subcutaneous priming and intranasal boosting in mice, highly loaded HA-decorated vaults induced significantly higher HA-specific serum IgG, IgG1, IgG2a, and IgA titers than soluble HA. Covalent attachment of HA to vaults also resulted in significantly higher IgG2a titers than the non-conjugated mixture of vaults and HA, reaching levels similar to those induced by CpG-adjuvanted HA. Despite the strong HA-specific antibody responses, anti-vault IgG titers remained low. Our approach adds high-density, adjustable antigen display to the established cargo-loading and targeting capabilities of human vaults, offering the possibility of combining all three functions in a single vaccine particle.

items.title: Complex IV Subunit C15orf48 Integrates Electron Transport Chain Function with Amino Acid and Lipid Metabolism to Regulate Innate Immunity
items.blurb: Despite extensive recognition of immunometabolism in innate immune regulation, how mitochondrial bioenergetic and metabolic pathways in monocytes interface to control inflammatory responses remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover that C15orf48 (MOCCI/NMES1/COXFA4L3), an inflammation-associated mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) subunit, orchestrates electron transport chain (ETC) function, fatty acid oxidation (FAO), and branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) catabolism to control monocyte activation. Loss of C15orf48 globally and in monocytes confers host tolerance and resistance to bacterial pneumonia and LPS-induced endotoxemia, characterized by reduced inflammatory gene expression, cytokine secretion, and monocyte activation. Mechanistically, C15orf48 increases mitochondrial ROS production and maintains NAD pools, which in turn supports long-chain FAO and BCAA catabolism required for robust monocyte activation and inflammatory cytokine production. These findings define a mitochondrial CIV metabolic axis directed by C15orf48 as central to monocyte activation and innate immunity, filling a key knowledge gap in immunometabolic control and presenting new targets for therapy in infection and sepsis.

items.title: Disrupting translation in CA1 pyramidal cells blocks novelty-induced increases in population firing rate while preserving newly formed assemblies
items.blurb: Long-term memory depends upon the translation of the plasticity-related proteins required for synaptic consolidation. Whether learning-related changes in hippocampal CA1 coding and synchrony require local synaptic consolidation or reflect plasticity elsewhere remains unknown. We used the inducible protein kinase R (iPKR) chemogenetic system to downregulate cap-dependent translation in CaMKII-expressing dorsal CA1 neurons through intracerebral infusion of an actuator that activates the integrated stress response. Without chemogenetic activation, iPKR mice exhibited elevated pyramidal cell firing and reduced interneuron firing relative to wild-type mice. Infusion of the chemogenetic actuator suppressed c-Fos expression for at least 24 hours and blocked the novelty-related increase in firing observed following vehicle infusion. Nevertheless, other aspects of experience-dependent physiology persisted. Pyramidal cells active during novel exploration remained preferentially recruited into sharp-wave ripples (SPW-Rs) hours into a post-exposure consolidation period. Pairwise coincident activity patterns formed during novel exploration were also reactivated during SPW-Rs with magnitudes and temporal persistence comparable to vehicle sessions and wild-type mice without infusions. When mice returned five hours after exposure to a novel environment, the assemblies formed during translation disruption were also re-expressed at magnitudes comparable to those observed during repeated familiar-environment visits and following novel exploration under vehicle. These findings demonstrate that experience-dependent reorganization of CA1 pyramidal cell synchrony can survive disruption of plasticity-related protein production, whereas novelty-related changes in excitability are impaired. Therefore, SPW-R reactivation and cell assembly consolidation likely depend upon plasticity pathways outside of the eIF2-dependent signaling pathways in the CA1 pyramidal cells targeted by the iPKR system.

items.title: Time-resolved multi-omics reveals constitutive defense preparedness and early responses to soybean cyst nematode in wild soybean
items.blurb: Soybean (Glycine max), a versatile cash crop, is the largest global source of plant-based protein and second-largest source of vegetable oil. However, soybean cyst nematode (SCN; Heterodera glycines) is the most economically damaging pest of soybean worldwide, causing substantial yield losses annually. Currently, the effectiveness of widely deployed genetic resistance in soybean cultivars is increasingly challenged by evolving SCN populations; therefore, identifying new sources and mechanisms of SCN resistance is critical. Crop wild relatives, the ancestral or closely related wild species of domesticated crops, are rich sources of genetic diversity encompassing various beneficial traits, including pathogen resistance. In this study, we applied a comparative, multi-omics approach to examine the molecular mechanisms underlying SCN resistance in wild soybean (Glycine soja). We integrated transcriptomic, metabolomic, and proteomic data from two wild soybean genotypes representing contrasting responses to SCN (S54, resistant; S67, susceptible) at early- and late-stage infection. Our results reveal distinct constitutive molecular profiles and contrasting genotype-specific responses to SCN infection. The resistant genotype S54 exhibited a stronger early transcriptional response, particularly involving defense signaling and stress-responsive processes, whereas the susceptible genotype S67 showed a delayed response. Gene co-expression and integrative multi-omics analyses identified coordinated molecular networks associated with resistance, including defense-related genes and metabolic features. Together, these findings suggest that SCN resistance in wild soybean involves both pre-existing molecular differences and early activation of defense-associated responses. Our work identifies candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for future functional testing. Ultimately, these findings provide an integrated multi-omics view of SCN resistance mechanisms in wild soybean, extending our understanding beyond commonly studied cultivar-based resistance and offering potential targets for soybean improvement.

items.title: The relationship between heart rate variability and cerebral autoregulation at elevated intracranial pressure
items.blurb: Objective. Altered intracranial pressure (ICP) is a key biomarker for traumatic brain injury (TBI). However, obtaining ICP measurements is a highly invasive process. Heart rate variability (HRV) has demonstrated potential as a useful biomarker for ICP changes, but few studies have investigated the relationship between ICP changes and HRV. This work examines how HRV and ICP interact in cases of TBI and whether HRV metrics can be informative of the state of autoregulatory control at elevated ICP. Approach. Electrocardiogram signals were recorded in seven non-human primates under anesthesia. ICP changes were induced by means of fluid increase via a cannula in the ventricles. Time- and frequency-domain HRV metrics were calculated from ECG and correlated with physiological indicators including CPP, ICP, and pressure reactivity index (PRx). Main results. Results demonstrate that there is no direct linear relationship between HRV and ICP. PRx and HRV, however, revealed a significant group level relationship where the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN) increased after a clinically significant PRx threshold, implying that HRV may be more closely associated with TBIs in terms of autoregulatory changes rather than ICP changes. Significance. This study provides insights into changes in brain physiology in response to ICP increases by demonstrating the relationship between CAR and HRV. Further, this work draws attention to conflicting reports in the literature when interpreting the interaction between HRV and other physiological variables.

items.title: Humidity detection after blood feeding in ticks is required for oviposition site selection and egg survival
items.blurb: Immediately following a blood meal, the female tick must locate conditions that allow successful egg development. A contributing factor is that conditions must be sufficiently moist to prevent egg dehydration. Previous studies show that humidity detection occurs through the forelegs and that interference with this process leads to tick mortality; however, this effect has not been examined in fed tick stages. Here, we show that female ticks exhibit a distinct attraction to higher humidity, directing them to locations where they arrest and subsequently deposit eggs. Interference with humidity detection caused fed females to deposit eggs at RHs below the optimal range for egg viability. Evaluation of tick egg viability at cluster sizes of 1, 5, 50, and naturally laid clusters (over 500 eggs) in relation to varying relative humidities reveals that depositing clusters of eggs under higher humidity conditions is critical for viability (Egg viability remained low below 85% RH but increased substantially at higher humidity levels). We found that application of the repellent DEET (N,N-diethyl-meta-toluamide) disrupted this behavior. Field validation shows a drastic reduction in surviving larvae when females cannot detect humidity (mechanical or chemical inhibition) during egg deposition. These studies confirm that fed female ticks must detect a humid site after detachment from the host to ensure egg viability, and that disrupting this process could be an effective tick control strategy.

items.title: Influence of interindividual variability structures on implied priors and population predictions in pharmacogenetic models
items.blurb: Interindividual variability (IIV) defines part of the prior distribution used in Bayesian parameter estimation. However, the dependence of model-implied priors on IIV and covariate model specifications is rarely examined explicitly. We evaluated empirical support for pooled versus phenotype-specific IIV structures and their consequences for predictive distributions in a CYP2D6-dependent population pharmacokinetic model. Four variants of a published codeine-metabolite model were independently re-estimated in NONMEM using data from 997 patients, combining continuous activity-score or categorical CYP2D6 parameterizations with pooled or phenotype-specific IIV. Distributions of morphine formation clearance were simulated in mrgsolve with 10,000 virtual individuals per phenotype and model. Two controlled 2 x 2 simulations isolated the effects of IIV variance structure within each parameterization. Phenotype-specific IIV improved model fit under both parameterizations ({Delta}OFV -448.57 and -44.27, respectively). The corresponding IIV variance estimates for poor metabolizers were 5.79 and 0.355. ETA variance shrinkage exceeded 90% in poor and ultrarapid metabolizers under both phenotype-specific IIV models. The four fitted models differed in the central tendency and dispersion of predicted morphine formation clearance. In controlled simulations, phenotype-specific IIV increased the coefficient of variation of morphine formation clearance in poor metabolizers approximately threefold under the continuous parameterization and by approximately 40% under the categorical parameterization. Both IIV estimates and their effects on population predictions depended on CYP2D6 parameterization. Importantly, improved model fit alone does not establish the biological validity of these distributions, and their implications for individual Bayesian posterior predictions remain to be evaluated.

items.title: Elucidating the membrane-binding mechanism of the ALPS-like motif of the Osh4 protein
items.blurb: Transport of lipids within cells is crucial for cellular functions and is facilitated by lipid transport proteins, like the Saccharomyces cerevisiae oxysterol-binding homologue (Osh) proteins. Among these, Osh4 is of particular interest, due to its role in lipid trafficking at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and trans-Golgi network (TGN). Here, we elucidate the membrane-binding mechanism of the amphipathic lipid packing sensor (ALPS)-like motif of Osh4 using circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) integrated with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Our findings show environment-dependent structural changes of the ALPS peptide, including a preference for -helical structure in the presence of phospholipid membranes which is modestly enhanced in the presence of anionic lipids. Fluorescence spectroscopy and MD simulation results corroborate the ALPS peptide's interaction with model membranes and reveal slightly enhanced binding to membranes containing anionic lipids. Moreover, XRD demonstrated the peptide influences membrane structure, with thinning observed upon peptide incorporation. We determined the binding affinity of the ALPS peptide to model membranes using ITC, which supports enthalpy-driven contributions between anionic lipids and the lysine in the ALPS peptide and an entropic contribution from serine and threonine residues desolvating into the membrane. Comparison with computational estimates using potential of mean force calculations suggests current force fields overestimate binding energy. Overall, our results support that the ALPS-like motif will preferentially bind to the TGN cytosolic leaflet, which contains a higher concentration of anionic lipids compared to the ER, providing insight into lipid transport by Osh4.

items.title: CellTouch: Learning to separate touching nuclei in anisotropic 3D cell cultures
items.blurb: 3D-oids, such as spheroids and organoids, are essential models in drug discovery and precision medicine, and quantitative analysis requires every nucleus to be segmented separately. Accurate 3D instance segmentation remains challenging, because nuclei are densely packed and touching, and volumes are sampled more coarsely along the Z-axis than laterally. Most existing methods were developed for near-isotropic data and tend to merge neighbouring nuclei. To address this challenge, we propose CellTouch, a deep learning method for anisotropic 3D nuclei instance segmentation that predicts flow fields and a contact channel, which separates touching nuclei directly from the network output. Ablations showed that the contact channel is the key design element, and CellTouch outperformed state-of-the-art methods on in-house data and widely used public datasets. Most importantly, dense Z-sampling is not required: CellTouch segmented nuclei as accurately at a 2 um Z-step as at 0.5 um, reducing acquisition time and data volume four-fold.

items.title: GNEval: A Context-Specific Benchmark for Gene Network Inference with Single-Cell Foundation Models
items.blurb: Gene network (GN) inference plays a critical role in understanding gene relationships and their roles in biological functions and diseases. Existing single-cell GN inference methods often rely on limited data from individual studies. Single-cell foundation models, pretrained on large and diverse datasets, provide a range of gene-gene association signals that offer a promising basis for GN inference. However, it remains unclear which GN properties these signals capture and how they compare with domain-specific methods. To address this gap, we introduce GNEval, a unified benchmark for evaluating pretrained model derived gene associations for network inference. We benchmark 21 gene representations and association scores from 11 models, including static gene embeddings (S), contextual embeddings (C), and gene-gene attention scores (A). GNEval assesses inferred networks based on their consistency with functional and perturbational evidence, including 14 Perturb-seq datasets across diverse cell systems, perturbation types and data sizes. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across evaluation tasks and models. Rankings based on Gene Ontology and Perturb-seq evidence were nearly uncorrelated (Spearman {rho} = -0.05). Context-independent representations showed a substantial advantage in recovering functional relationships ({Delta}AUROC = 0.13), whereas context-dependent gene associations improved recovery of perturbation-associated differential expression relationships by 3.8x. The domain-specific method achieves relatively strong performance on both evidence types, offering a better balance across the two evaluations than most foundation-model-derived networks. Overall, gene representations and association scores show task-specific strengths, highlighting the need for task-aware selection and integration with domain-specific methods.

items.title: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
items.blurb: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references. Baseline-relative representations improved held-out-donor prediction with both State SE and scFoundation. Across independent perturbation datasets, CYTAP prioritized applied cytokines, including when receptor transcripts were sparsely detected, and ranked administered cytokines among the top ten in both in vivo datasets. In an unpaired COVID-19 cohort, inferred responses were associated with severity, and IL-6 response scores correlated with plasma IL-6 concentrations. These findings support the use of biologically defined references to adapt pretrained representations for functional response inference.

items.title: EHRMENEIA: A Benchmark for Foundation Models on Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.blurb: Electronic health record foundation models are evaluated using heterogeneous targets, vocabularies, and adaptation procedures, preventing systematic characterization across model families. We introduce EHRMENEIA (https://ehrmeneia.upc.edu/), a benchmark that provides a multidimensional evaluation framework for next-event prediction, multi-horizon event occurrence, trajectory fidelity and few-shot representation transfer. EHRMENEIA preserves each model's native vocabulary and temporal representation while mapping clinical outputs to shared evaluation objects. Applied to two released clinical checkpoints and two synthetic demonstrations, the framework exposed substantial differences not only in performance but in the clinical questions that could be evaluated from each model--dataset interface. EHRMENEIA introduces a view of benchmarking in which the supported clinical evaluation domain is identified before performance within that domain is interpreted. The framework therefore shifts foundation-model benchmarking from scalar ranking toward characterization of what can, and cannot, be inferred from model outputs.

items.title: A Benchmark for Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Enzyme Kinetic Parameters of Metabolic Networks
items.blurb: Large-scale kinetic models predict how metabolism responds to genetic and environmental perturbations, but building them at scale is limited by the scarcity of experimentally determined enzyme kinetic parameters. Generative machine learning has been proposed to address this bottleneck, yet prior work has each introduced a single, bespoke architecture, leaving open which generative paradigm suits this problem and why. We introduce a benchmark suite for generative modeling of high-dimensional enzyme kinetic parameter sets: labeled datasets of kinetically feasible Escherichia coli models paired with a mechanistically grounded evaluation harness that scores generated ensembles on dynamical stability and agreement with experimentally observed phenotypes, rather than statistical realism alone. Using it, we compare three standard architectures at matched capacity, a conditional variational autoencoder, a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty, and a RealNVP normalizing flow, each under two conditioning schemes (a discrete high/low label and a continuous, graded key-performance-indicator target), across a difficulty ladder from one mutant phenotype to a stringent class of nine reproduced jointly. Two findings stand out. The architectures trace a consistent concentration-exploration trade-off, the VAE concentrating, the flow exploring and extrapolating, the GAN in between, but this ordering is overturned at high stringency by the conditioning scheme: at the joint class, continuous targets reach 33 to 117-fold enrichment over random sampling for every architecture, whereas discrete labels stay at 1.3 to 15-fold. Beyond the comparison, the suite is an accessible, mechanistically validated reference task for groups outside the kinetic-modeling community to benchmark their own generative algorithms.

items.title: Reference genomes for Australian Cryptosporidium hominis and C. parvum from humans
items.blurb: Cryptosporidium hominis and C. parvum are important protozoan pathogens of humans worldwide, and genomic surveillance is increasingly being used to investigate transmission and outbreaks. However, no complete Cryptosporidium genome is available from Australia, and many common Cryptosporidium gp60 subtypes lack high-quality genome assemblies worldwide. This study generated the first Australian reference genomes for two clinically relevant, zoonotic Cryptosporidium species, C. hominis and C. parvum from human hosts, as well as a scaffold-level genome for Australian C. meleagridis. Oocysts were purified from eleven clinical faecal samples and whole-genome sequencing was performed using short-read technologies. Three samples belonging to different species were also sequenced using long-read technology, with assemblies generated, telomere recovery undertaken and genomes annotated. High-quality reference C. hominis IaA12R3 genome (8 T2T chromosomes, 9.2 Mb, 4069 genes, 98.4% completeness), near-complete C. parvum IIaA20G3R1 genome (8 chromosomes, 9.2 Mb, 4004 genes, 98.2% completeness), and a draft C. meleagridis IIIgA31 genome (113 scaffolds, 9.3 Mb, 4075 genes, 97.2% completeness) were generated and had high nucleotide similarity (98-99%), gene cluster orthology (99%) and genome synteny relative to available international reference genomes. Phylogenomic analyses with global C. hominis and C. parvum genomes were performed to characterise the relationships of Australian isolates globally showing Australian C. hominis and C. parvum forming well-supported clades with North American European isolates. Whole-genome analyses of eight Australian C. hominis isolates revealed markedly better resolution of genetic relationships than gp60 subtyping alone. This study provides the resources for national genomic surveillance in Australia and expands the genomic representation of clinically relevant Cryptosporidium subtypes. Broader application of genomic surveillance has the potential to enhance outbreak investigation, improve understanding of transmission dynamics and support One Health approaches to cryptosporidiosis control.

items.title: Trade-offs between sexual and clonal reproduction differ within versus among populations
items.blurb: Plants exhibit large variation in reproductive strategies, from obligately sexual to exclusively asexual. Clonal vegetative reproduction is common among plants, and despite theory assuming that trade-offs exist between sexual and clonal reproduction, empirical demonstrations of trade-offs remain elusive. Here we examined whether the strength of genotypic trade-offs in white clover (Trifolium repens) depends on spatial scale of sampling, and the environmental factors that favour sexual versus clonal reproduction. We quantified genetic variation and tested for trade-offs within and among populations from North America. Within a population, we grew up to 5 clonal replicates from each of 38 genotypes collected from a population in southern Canada. Among populations, we grew up to 5 clonal replicates from each of 46 populations, collected from a 21{o} transect from southern USA to northern Canada. All plants were randomized in a single growth chamber and grown for 12 weeks while keeping resource availability constant. From each plant, we measured investment in sexual reproduction as the number of inflorescences, and investment in clonal reproduction as the number of stolons, total stolon length and leaf area. We also extracted multiple environmental variables from each population. There was substantial genetic variation for all traits at both spatial scales, but genetic variation was always greater among populations. At the within population scale, the number of inflorescences was positively genetically correlated with the number of stolons and leaf area. Among populations, the number of inflorescences was negatively genetically correlated with both stolon length and leaf area. Colder, drier, high-latitude sites were associated with increased clonality. Our results show that the strength and direction of genotypic trade-offs differs within versus among populations, with trade-offs only being apparent at the largest scale among populations. These results provide insight into when and how trade-offs evolve between sexual and clonal plant reproductive strategies.

items.title: Contrasting taxonomic and functional diversity of tropical anuran communities across crude oil-contaminated and reference streams in a biodiversity hotspot
items.blurb: Conservation assessments of chronic anthropogenic disturbance increasingly ask whether changes in species composition translate into comparable changes in ecological function. This distinction is central to anticipating the long-term consequences of disturbance for ecosystem processes. Crude oil spills are a recurrent but understudied source of chronic disturbance in tropical freshwater ecosystems. We evaluated whether chronic oil contamination is associated with changes in taxonomic and functional diversity of anuran communities in six streams of the Narino coastal piedmont (Colombian Choco), within the area of influence of the Trans-Andean Pipeline. Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrate group worldwide and are particularly sensitive to both aquatic and terrestrial habitat degradation, making them sensitive indicators of chronic disturbance. We compared three oil-contaminated and three reference streams using standardized nocturnal surveys, Hill-number diversity, beta diversity, and multidimensional functional traits. We recorded 169 individuals from 24 species. Reference streams collectively contained more species and individuals than oil-contaminated streams, although coverage-standardized diversity varied substantially among individual streams and confidence intervals broadly overlapped. In contrast, functional diversity metrics, including functional richness, evenness, divergence, and trait composition, showed broad overlap between stream types. Overall, taxonomic patterns tended to favor reference streams, but these differences were not accompanied by a clear functional simplification, revealing a partial decoupling between taxonomic and functional responses consistent with high functional redundancy in one of the world's most biodiverse and chronically oil-exposed tropical regions. This decoupling underscores the need to incorporate functional, not only taxonomic, metrics into biodiversity impact assessments of chronic contamination in biodiversity hotspots.

items.title: A human-accelerated enhancer rewires FOXC1-dependent skeletal development
items.blurb: The evolution of human skeletal morphology involved modifications to conserved developmental programs, but the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we integrate single-cell transcriptomic atlases of developing human, macaque and mouse limbs with comparative chromatin interaction maps of chondrocytes. We identify human-biased transcriptional programs within conserved osteochondral lineages and link divergent chromatin interactions to human-specific sequence changes. These analyses identify zooHAR.30, a human accelerated region that contacts the promoter of FOXC1, a key regulator of skeletal development. Human-specific substitutions within zooHAR.30 alter transcription factor binding, and the human sequence exhibits enhanced regulatory activity in chondrocytes and more spatially restricted activity in the developing limb, predominantly in the zeugopod, compared with the chimpanzee ortholog. Replacing the endogenous human sequence with its chimpanzee ortholog reduces FOXC1 and GMDS expression, impairs cell proliferation and osteochondral differentiation, and alters FOXC1 occupancy across skeletal regulatory elements, including a GDF5 enhancer implicated in knee morphology and osteoarthritis. Our findings reveal how evolutionary changes in a single enhancer can propagate through a conserved developmental regulatory network, providing a mechanistic link between human-specific sequence divergence and the evolution of skeletal developmental programs.

items.title: Characterization of Natural Killer Cell-Associated Prognostic Signature Reveals Immune Landscape and Prognostic Value in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (UCEC)
items.blurb: Background: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical in eliminating virus-infected and cancer cells. Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is a common malignancy in women, and the role of NK cells in UCEC has attracted significant attention. This study aims to develop an NK cell-related gene signature (NRGs) to improve immunotherapy response and prognosis evaluation in UCEC. Methods: Consensus clustering classified UCEC samples based on NRGs. Univariate Cox regression, differential expression, and Lasso regression were used to build a prognostic model. Differences in tumor microenvironment (TME), immune checkpoints, and clinical features were compared between high- and low-risk groups. Results: High NK cell infiltration was associated with a favorable prognosis. Eleven key NRGs were identified, and consensus clustering divided patients into two clusters: Cluster 1 (C1) had better prognosis and higher immune cell infiltration. A nine-NRG signature (CEACAM1, IFNG, PTPN6, KNSTRN, XCL1, IL2RG, RAC3, MICB, CCL3) was developed. The high-risk group had more advanced-stage cases, higher-grade tumors, and serous carcinoma compared to the low-risk group (P < 0.05). Conclusions: The 9-NRGs signature demonstrates strong predictive performance and offers valuable insights for future immuno-oncology research.

items.title: The Metaphor Zoo by Jeremy Butterfield review – how animals influence our language
items.blurb:
A lexicographer reveals the surprising origins of common zoological turns of phrase, from fat cats to fur babies

Anyone who has grown up in the country knows that cows come home. They do it at tea time, like clockwork, because an unmilked cow is an uncomfortable cow. So how did “till the cows come home” come to mean never? Stranger still, when the phrase first appears in a 1587 commentary on St Paul’s epistle to the Galatians, there is only one cow. By the time playwrights Beaumont and Fletcher take it up a few decades later, their characters are kissing and drinking till the cow – still single – comes home. What began as a promise of endless pleasure has become a sigh of futility.

Jeremy Butterfield’s Metaphor Zoo is full of such linguistic metamorphoses. Butterfield is a lexicographer by trade, the man the OUP entrusted with revising Fowler’s Modern English Usage. His guiding text is Lakoff and Johnson’s Metaphors We Live By (1980), which argues that metaphors don’t just colour how we speak but structure our thinking. In this sprightly but well-grounded book (metaphor alert), Butterfield asks what mental patterns lie behind the hundreds of animal phrases in English. Then in Johnsonian fashion, he sets about tracing the original, dating each through the Oxford English Dictionary and watching as it goes walkabout.

items.title: The Guardian view on AI and the Riemann hypothesis: a triumph of intelligence, a test of democracy | Editorial
items.blurb:
Machines are solving problems that have been beyond the reach of human ingenuity. Their growing power must not become the sole preserve of billionaires

For the average person, the news that AI has helped crack a problem that has defied mathematicians since 1859 might elicit momentary awe. What ought to worry everyone is not the discovery per se, but what it says about the power of the machines making it. The pace of scientific discovery looks like it is outrunning the ability of humanity – and its institutions – to understand, let alone regulate, AI’s advances.

Last Friday Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, said that he, with the assistance of an unreleased version of the company’s Claude chatbot, had produced what many mathematicians see as the holy grail: a proof for the Riemann hypothesis. Mathematicians like Cornell University’s Steven Strogatz had already cried on podcasts, lamenting that students were asking: “What’s the point if the AI can do math better than any human being?” Computers can validate the Alpöge-Claude proof. But Prof Strogatz fears AI’s discoveries may soon defy human understanding. Asking AI to explain them, he said, would be like him trying to teach calculus to his own dog.

One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished.

But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two top records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more.

items.title: South Sudan Humanitarian Fund: 2026 monitoring report (1 January to 31 August 2026)
items.blurb:
Countries: South Sudan, Sudan
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached file.

South Sudan Humanitarian Fund: 2026 monitoring report (1 January to 31 August 2026)

The South Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SSHF) monitored 87 projects implemented by 54 partners from 1 January to 31 August 2026. The report describes how partners delivered assistance and managed funds, what delayed delivery and how the Fund follows up on problems it finds.

At a glance

  • 87 projects monitored: 43 implemented by national non-governmental organizations, 33 by international non-governmental organizations and 11 by United Nations agencies
  • 54 implementing partners: 30 national non-governmental organizations, 19 international non-governmental organizations and five United Nations agencies
  • 142 monitoring exercises: 77 field visits, 20 remote assessments (11 calls and nine surveys) and 45 on-site financial spot-checks

What the monitoring found

SSHF rated 71 of 97 field visits and remote assessments (73 per cent) good or outstanding. In 23 assessments, operating conditions justified underperformance. In two, the justification was insufficient. In one, no project activity had taken place at the time of monitoring. These ratings reflect what monitors found at the time of each assessment. For an overall assessment of project performance, the Fund also considers financial spot-checks, partner reports, cluster reports and other evidence.

SSHF rated 38 of 45 financial spot-checks (84 per cent) good or outstanding. Six found underperformance with sufficient justification and one without. The checks identified gaps in supporting documents, procurement procedures, personnel records, expenditure coding and internal controls. In one case, a payment voucher lacked a delivery note and a goods received note. A follow-up spot-check confirmed that the partner had filed both documents with the voucher.

Community committees helped partners identify people in need of assistance and resolve disputes. Providing health, nutrition, protection and water, sanitation and hygiene services together improved access and referrals. Mobile teams helped reach displaced people and remote communities. Delayed or incomplete supplies disrupted delivery. Flooding and insecurity restricted access, delayed construction and raised costs. Inflation reduced what people could buy with cash assistance.

Follow-up

The Fund will work with clusters and supply agencies to address delays, train national partners in financial management and reporting, track corrective actions, improve monitoring data and documentation, and complete the remaining monitoring planned for 2026. It will use the findings to inform partner risk assessments, project revisions and future funding allocations.

items.title: Somalia: Radio Ergo Weekly Feedback Report, Issued: 27 Nov 2026
items.blurb:
Country: Somalia
Source: Radio Ergo

Please refer to the attached file.

Brief Summary

Commentary on rainfall and its positive impact on lives and livelihoods continued to form the bulk of the calls to Radio Ergo’s nationwide feedback platform in the week 19-25 November 2026. These calls came mostly from Jubbaland, South West, Hirshabelle, and some from Galmudug. However, some callers mainly in southern locations noted a tailing off of the rainfall, patchy areas without rain, and also intensely hot temperatures. A few in Gedo and Bay regions said they were now running short of water again. Drought conditions were cited in Bari. Several callers complained about influxes of mosquitoes and rising malaria cases, and wanted mosquito control measures. In Gedo region a number of IDP callers complained of hardships and their need for aid. The following summarises the calls by theme.

Health – callers in Awdhegle in Lower Shabelle and Adado in Galgadud spoke of influxes of mosquitoes in their areas and a rise in malaria and wanted the menace to be brought under control. A caller in Gedo said the mosquitoes were causing illness with headaches and fever. A caller in Bardera said they had good rainfall, but mosquitoes were their main concern. A caller in Dollow also cited a mosquito influx, adding that despite the rain people were impoverished and aid agencies hadn’t visited the area for six months.

IDPs – a caller in Iftin camp, Bardera, said they and their farms were doing well after the rain. On the other hand, a female caller in Bardera identifying as an IDP said they had received little rainfall, their crops had been attacked by pests and disease, and the schools had been shut for the past six months depriving the children of education. In Qurdubey, a caller called twice on behalf of displaced families who had lost their livestock. He said those families with a few livestock left were able to sell them for a living, but others like them were facing hardship and challenging conditions including poor sanitation. He added an appeal for aid.

Aid – a caller in Dollow complained that they had been registered by aid groups a few days ago, but had not received the cash aid they thought they were going to get. Another caller, location unspecified, wanted a resumption of the cash aid they used to get from WFP that had stopped.

Food Security – a caller in Bardera said he wanted to share information about the high inflation and rising costs of basics they were facing.

Locusts – a caller in Kismayo said he had a farm near the airport and was concerned about locusts. He wanted to know how the farmers could protect their crops.

Climate – a caller in Baidoa, Bay region, said they’d been experiencing intense heat and wanted to know if this was because of climate change. Similarly, a caller in Bahdo, Galgadud, said recent days had been intensely hot and people wondered if it was a sign of rain to come, or of climate change. Other callers in Guriel, Dollow, and Kismayo also described intense heat in their areas.

Agriculture – farmers in southern and some central areas complained of pests damaging a range of produce including potatoes, beans, sesame, sorghum, maize, lettuce and tomatoes. They wanted to talk with experts on Radio Ergo’s weekly farming programme.

Livestock – a caller in Bardera said his camels had dukan (trypanosomiasis) and the medicine he was injecting them with was not working. He wanted veterinary advice. Several herders in Jubbaland complained of foot and mouth affecting their herds. A caller in Beletweyne wanted to know more about how pre-export livestock inspections and certifications were processed in Somalia.

Drought & water shortage – a caller in Rako-raho, Bari region, said they faced drought in the area and that many people had already migrated away. He added that they were in a desperate situation and needed the Puntland authority to reach them with aid. One caller in Dusamareb said they faced drought and conflict. Several in Bay region said the rain had been poor or had stopped already, with one describing the drying up of crops and grazing. A caller in Bardera said rainfall had been little and their farms were failing due to water shortages. A female caller said that odder and water shortage were affecting their livestock. Another female caller in Lower Juba said they weren’t having rainfall, the heat was intense, and their livestock were struggling.

Rainfall – a female caller in Farjeni, Bari, said they had received some light rain. A caller in Harardhere, Mudug, said they were getting heavy rain and doing well. In Galgadud, callers spoke of decent rain in Bahdo, Guriel, Abudwak, and Adado, with several noting intense heat. In Hiran, callers in Buleburte, Af-ad, and El-gal noted good rain and conditions for their livestock and farms. Callers in Baidoa, Burhakaba, and Dinsor in Bay region cited beneficial rain. One in Bakool said the rain was short-lived and they hoped for more. In Gedo, several in different districts said they had had good rain but that in some places it had stopped. A caller in Tulo-banan said the rain was good, although they were poor and there were no jobs. A number of callers in Kismayo cited beneficial rainfall helping crops and livestock, while some noted dry areas nearby.
